claim: For 0<omega<1, 1<q<2 and the real Lorentz sequence plane d^(2)(omega,q) with norm (max(|x1|,|x2|)^q+omega min(|x1|,|x2|)^q)^(1/q), put rho=omega^(1/(2-q)). The exact Ptolemy constant of its dual is (1+rho^2)^((2-q)/q) max{1,2/(1+omega)^(2/q)}. By the previously known primal and endpoint calculations, the primal and dual constants agree for every 0<omega<1, 1<=q<infinity.
integrity: The dual support-function optimization over x1>=x2>=0 gives N*(M,m)=(M^p+omega^(1-p)m^p)^(1/p) for m<=omega M and (M+m)/(1+omega)^(1/q) otherwise (p=q/(q-1)). The ratio to Euclidean norm has unique first-branch minimum at rho=omega^(1/(2-q)), and maximum at the axis or diagonal. Euclidean Ptolemy yields (b/a)^2, attained by explicitly constructed triples in both weight regimes. Parameter endpoints and the phase boundary are treated as stated.
scientific_limitations: The new computation is real, two-dimensional and 1<q<2. The all-exponent equality uses already established boundary and q>=2 cases. No claim for dimension>2 or complex spaces.
title: Exact Ptolemy constant of dual two-dimensional Lorentz spaces below exponent two
